items.title: Muggsy Spanier Interview, 1961-02-02
items.q: I heard him in late years. Oh, he was a wonderful fellow. He was a timid soul. He was very nice.

ctx.x: Yeah, I'd play the Dippermouth Blues and the Riverside Blues and all those tunes. I knew all those tunes. Joe would get a big kick out of it when I'd play the Dippermouth Blues because it's not the Dippermouth Blues unless you play it like Joe.

That's right. Yeah, you still got all that down the same. Oh, yeah. Same words. How did Johnny Dodds impress you? Sometimes he sounds a little rough on records and other times he sounds so great. I just wondered how was he in person in those days? I heard him in late years. Oh, he was a wonderful fellow.

He was a timid soul. He was very nice. I liked his planet playing very much. I believe he used to, you'd think he was afraid of a microphone. And Joe Oliver, he was afraid of a microphone too. He didn't like a microphone. Really? Didn't like? I don't either.
